response.summary: I found no material defect in the current Codex rules. Both round-1 findings are resolved, and so is the round-1 concern about the seven-column strip. The old 380px viewport cutoff has been removed (lines 435-442 now hold only the earlier non-calendar rules). In its place, `.week{container-type:inline-size}` and two container queries in rem units sit at `style.css:443-454`. Their layout rules come later in the file than the media-query rules and have the same specificity, so they override them only when the condition matches. The host's `calendar-internal-report.json` covers 320, 360, 380, 384, 388, 390, 641, 700, 720 and 1048px, each at scale 1 and 2. In every case the page is no wider than the viewport, and every day-name, date and note has scrollWidth equal to clientWidth. F1 is resolved: at 384 and 388px with 200% text the notes move to their own row (for example 'No session' at 49–182px inside a 36–348px day). F2 is resolved: at 320px with 100% text the three-column list stays (Sat 43px, 24 at 99px, note at 145px), and with 200% text the date stays next to the weekday (Sat ends at 89px, 24 starts at 147px) with the note on the row below. F3 is resolved: at 700, 720 and 1048px with 200% text the strip switches to the contained list, and at 100% the seven-column notes stay inside their cells (700px: Sun cell 130.8–213.7px, note wraps at 140.8–188.1px). Keyboard order and day selection are unaffected. The DOM order in `daysHTML` (`app.js:83`) is unchanged, `grid-column` doesn't reorder anything, and the arrow-key handler (`app.js:160`) accepts both axes, so it works in either orientation. Nothing hides overflow and no font size is reduced. The one remaining item is a low-severity cosmetic issue in the earlier Claude-authored seven-column layout.

findings.evidence: The inline-block event dot only applies when the 36rem container query matches (line 449). Above that width the note is still the original inline-flex with wrapping (line 214), and the dot and the text are separate flex items. With 100% text the text doesn't fit beside the dot, so the dot ends up alone on its own line. In `calendar-internal-report.json` at 700px, scale 1, the Mon note's rects are the dot at 229.7–237.7px, then 'Session' starting again at 229.7px on the next line. At 1048px, scale 1, the note runs over three lines with the dot alone at 491.2–499.2px. Nothing overflows or is clipped; it only looks odd, and it comes from the earlier design, not the new rules.
findings.fix: Optional: apply `.day-note{display:block}` and `.day-note .eventdot{display:inline-block;margin-right:7px}` unconditionally, not just inside the 36rem query, so the dot stays on the same line as the first word of 'Session' in every layout.

coverage: `style.css:435-456`: the current end-of-file rules. I confirmed the old 380px calendar rules are gone and checked the `.week` container and both container queries for specificity and source order against the `.day`/`.days` media rules at lines 209-222, 373-381, 388-393, 399-411.
`style.css:188`: `.desk-lower` grid tracks (minmax(0,…)/minmax(320px,…)). Inline-size containment on `.week` can't collapse the card in these tracks.
`app.js:83, 85, 129, 160`: day markup, selectDay, the click handler and the arrow/Home/End key handler. All are unaffected by CSS-only layout changes.

`calendar-internal-report.json`: page width vs. viewport and per-text client/scroll widths for every case (320, 360, 380, 384, 388, 390, 641, 700, 720, 1048 × scale 1/2). I read the full per-text bounds and rects for 320, 360, 380, 384 and 388 (scale 1 and 2), and the opening day entries for 700 and 1048 at scale 1. For 390–1048 at scale 2, I checked only that each note's width is 133/170px, the same as the stacked-row cases.
Round-1 findings F1, F2 and F3 rechecked against the new measurements.
limitations: Read-only: I didn't render anything or run tests. My conclusions rely on the host-produced measurement report and on reading the CSS.
I didn't open the new `calendar-*-text200.png` screenshots this round. I relied on the internal report, which measures text bounds directly.

I can't tell how the capture applies 'scale 2' (root font-size vs. browser text-size setting). In both cases rem in container queries follows the root font-size, but I haven't checked page zoom or iOS Dynamic Type.
Browsers without container-query support ignore these rules and fall back to the earlier media-query layout, which overflows with enlarged text. I didn't test on older browsers.
Only 1–2 rem-equivalent scales were measured. I checked intermediate scales such as 125% and 150% only by arithmetic, which shows comfortable margins.
This review doesn't claim independence over the earlier Claude-authored design.
